progression.prerequisiteKnowledge: The first video of this series: clone, alleles, variation, asexual copying is fast and alike while sexual reproduction is slow and varied, and the Cavendish banana as a clone with one shared weakness. The plant reproduction video: anthers make pollen, a stigma receives it, a pollen tube carries sperm to the egg, pollination is not fertilisation, bags keep pollen out. The mammal videos: sperm must reach an egg and an egg is released at ovulation. Not assumed: selective breeding, artificial insemination, artificial pollination, gene pool, semen, being on heat, rust, evaluate, criteria.
progression.startsWith: A dairy farmer who wants calves from a bull that lives hours away, and a wheat breeder who wants the yield of one variety and the rust resistance of another.
progression.stopsAfter: Saying what artificial insemination and artificial pollination do and which reproduction knowledge each depends on; saying why copying a winner gives a uniform crop and a shared weakness; defining evaluate as making a judgement using criteria and using gain, variety, cost and welfare as a good start; building a model Evaluate answer with a judgement, gain with evidence, variety, cost and welfare, and a weighing with a verdict that says when; applying the same reasoning to an unseen sheep case and an unseen plant fault.
progression.nextLesson: DNA structure and semi-conservative replication: how a cell copies its DNA, the step behind every clone and every egg and sperm.

teaching.task: Explain how farmers use knowledge of reproduction to improve animals and crops, and evaluate the gain and the cost of each method.
teaching.causalExplanation: Artificial insemination works because an egg is ready for only a short time around ovulation, so semen that is collected, split into doses and usually frozen can be placed in the cow during heat from a bull on any farm. Artificial pollination works because anthers make pollen, pollen landing on a stigma leads to a pollen tube that carries sperm to the egg, and bags keep other pollen out. Both speed up improvement by picking few parents, and the same reach narrows the gene pool, so one disease can reach every animal or plant, and chasing one trait can harm another. A good evaluation weighs the gain, the variety, the cost and the welfare and says when the method is worth it.
teaching.conversationalApproach: Opens on two farmers with a wish and a distance or a disease, shows what each person does with their hands before naming the method, fills one scorecard of gain, variety, cost and welfare across the three methods, then names evaluate and builds a model answer one card at a time before an unseen sheep and wheat case.
teaching.openingDecision: A dairy farmer wants calves from the best bull in the country and a wheat breeder wants yield and rust resistance in one plant. How could each of them use what we know about reproduction, and how would you judge whether it is worth the cost?
teaching.understandingCheck: Give one benefit, one ten-year risk and one change that keeps the benefit for a sheep farmer using one champion ram, and name why many seedlings are not resistant and two steps that fix it when a wheat breeder places pollen on open flowers of a plant that pollinates itself.
teaching.curriculumScope: Evaluate the impact of scientific knowledge on the manipulation of plant and animal reproduction in agriculture (Module 5). Embryo transfer, general selective breeding, DNA and the nucleus, cloning of animals and the 6-mark Assess question are held back.

design.visualSystem: Explainer engine: warm paper stage, handwritten Caveat headings, amber doodle layer, painted dairy bull and cow, wheat ear and floret, and wheat leaf with rust plates beside coded straws, freezer, cycle strip, gene pool bead tray, scorecard, model answer cards, attempt boards and countdown. Colour key: green gain, blue variety, amber cost, rose welfare, flat grey tags for risks so nothing reads as a score.
design.transitionPlan: The hook plates slide in side by side; the bull plate stays while the straw route draws; the tract outline enlarges for the timing scene; the scorecard and gene pool tray appear in the gain and risk scene and stay in the same positions; the camera pushes into one wheat floret; the flower cutaway crossfades in as a recall; the potato and banana plates crossfade in; the scorecard enlarges for the evaluate scene and cards stack for the model answer; the attempt board removes the scorecard and tray and they return in the feedback and memory scenes; scene crossfade with settle.

scenes.visualReference: Painted dairy bull and cow pair on the left, the wheat leaf plate (rust beside healthy) and the wheat ear plate on the right, a coded map chip and two small trait chips
scenes.teachingReason: Poses two linked questions on two real farmers: how each gets what they want, then how to judge whether it is worth it
scenes.narrationCue: wants her calves fathered by the best bull in the country / hours away / Rust is a fungal disease of wheat / how would you judge whether it is worth the cost
scenes.motionPurpose: A dashed line draws between the two farms, a ring marks the rust spots, two trait chips point to one wheat ear with a question mark, and the heading holds on its question
scenes.onScreenChange: The bull and cow plate fills the left; a map chip draws a dashed line on "hours away"; the rust leaf plate shows a scribble circle on the pustules on "Rust is a fungal disease of wheat"; the ear plate slides in with "high yield" and "rust resistant" chips arrowing to one ear; the heading writes on and its second half writes on "worth the cost"
scenes.holdPurpose: Hold on the question mark for about two seconds

scenes.visualReference: Bull plate at the left, coded collection vial, straws, freezer icon and a coded cutaway of the cow's reproductive tract with a thin tube
scenes.teachingReason: Shows what the farmer does, step by step, before the name artificial insemination is used again as a label
scenes.narrationCue: artificial insemination / collected, diluted and split into many small doses / usually frozen / any farm / thaws one dose
scenes.motionPurpose: The vial fills and splits into a row of straws, frost spreads, one straw travels to the cow plate, thaws, and a thin tube carries the dose into the uterus
scenes.onScreenChange: The vial fills on "collected"; its contents divide into straws on "split into many small doses"; a frost wash and an opening freezer icon appear on "usually frozen"; a dot carries one straw along a dashed route on "any farm"; the frost fades and a thin tube draws into the cow's tract outline on "thaws one dose"
scenes.holdPurpose: Brief hold on the dose reaching the uterus

scenes.visualReference: Enlarged cow tract outline, coded cycle strip with an on heat bar and a short green egg-ready arc, and a clock ring
scenes.teachingReason: Shows why timing matters: the egg is ready for only a short window, so the dose must be placed during heat
scenes.narrationCue: an egg ready for only a short time in each cycle / being on heat / about a day after it starts / during heat, before the egg is released
scenes.motionPurpose: The tract enlarges, a short green window draws on the cycle strip, an egg leaves the ovary, and a clock ring ticks across the heat bar before the dose is placed
scenes.onScreenChange: The tract outline enlarges; the cycle strip draws with a short green "egg ready" arc on "an egg ready for only a short time"; an egg dot leaves an ovary on "ovulation"; the label "on heat" writes over the heat bar with a ticking clock ring; the egg follows about a day later and the dose arrow lands inside the heat bar
scenes.holdPurpose: Hold the heat bar and the egg window together

scenes.visualReference: Coded scorecard (gain, variety, cost, welfare by method), gene pool tray of 24 beads in six colours with a herd of cow icons, a gentle rising line marked illustrative
scenes.teachingReason: Names the gain first, then shows with the tray how the same reach narrows the herd's variety
scenes.narrationCue: What does it gain? / a proven bull / the same reach is the risk / If a few bulls father most of the calves / one disease can spread through the whole herd
scenes.motionPurpose: The scorecard gains a green tick row, a rising line draws on, then one bead colour spreads through the tray until the herd shares it and a disease icon moves along the herd
scenes.onScreenChange: The scorecard appears with four rows; the gain row writes on with a green tick and the rising line draws on; the gene pool tray appears with six bead colours; the bull's orange bead spreads across the herd on "If a few bulls father most of the calves"; the variety row fills with a blue bead; a disease icon passes along the herd and lights each cow grey

scenes.visualReference: Source chip, three-step chain with a steepening line and a falling line (both illustrative), welfare heart and cost coin on the scorecard
scenes.teachingReason: Gives the fertility trade-off with its source, then fills welfare and cost on the scorecard
scenes.narrationCue: Studies of Holstein cows in several countries / the chance of becoming pregnant after each insemination fell / A cow that struggles to get pregnant can have a harder life on the farm / usually less than buying and keeping a top bull on every farm
scenes.motionPurpose: A source chip writes on, a three-step chain builds with one line steepening and another falling, a rose heart lands on welfare and an amber coin lands on cost
scenes.onScreenChange: The source chip writes on; the chain steps land one per spoken idea; the rising line steepens and a second short line falls; the welfare row writes on with a rose heart; an amber coin falls on the cost row on "Semen and a trained worker cost money" with the comparison note writing on

scenes.visualReference: Wheat ear plate with a camera push to one floret, coded forceps, bag and donor plant; scorecard shrunk to a chip
scenes.teachingReason: Shows what the breeder does with her hands before the technique has a name and why self-pollination must be stopped
scenes.narrationCue: artificial pollination / removes the anthers / rust-resistant plant / covers the flowers with a bag
scenes.motionPurpose: The camera pushes to the floret, forceps lift the anthers out, pollen from the donor plant travels to the stigma and a bag covers the ear
scenes.onScreenChange: A slow push reaches one open floret; a scribble circle lands on the anthers on "removes the anthers" and forceps lift them out; two tags mark the seed parent and the pollen parent; a pollen dot travels from the donor to the stigma; a coded bag draws over the ear on "covers the flowers with a bag"

scenes.visualReference: Flower cutaway plate (anther, stigma, pollen tube) as a recall, two plant icons sending dots to seeds, seedling rows with allele beads, and the second scorecard column
scenes.teachingReason: Ties the technique back to the pollen tube and sexual mixing, and shows the new variety takes generations
scenes.narrationCue: a tube carries sperm to the egg / Every seed has the two parents she picked / the alleles are mixed in new ways / only some plants show both traits / takes years of hand work
scenes.motionPurpose: The flower plate recalls the tube path, two parents send dots to a seed, identical first seedlings grow, then the next generation mixes and only some show both traits
scenes.onScreenChange: The cutaway plate crossfades in with anther, stigma and tube labels writing on in turn, then shrinks; green and gold plants send dots to a seed; three identical seedlings grow; the next row shows mixed bead pairs with only some ringed as showing both traits; the scorecard column gains gain and cost

scenes.visualReference: Gene pool tray in one colour, coded field of identical wheat plants with shield icons, coded Uganda pin and rust wash
scenes.teachingReason: Shows why growing one variety everywhere shares one weakness, with a sourced example
scenes.narrationCue: share the same defences / first found in Uganda in 1998 to 1999 / overcame a resistance gene
scenes.motionPurpose: The tray turns to one colour, a field of shielded plants fills the screen, a pin drops on Uganda, an orange wash spreads and the shields shatter
scenes.onScreenChange: The tray shows one colour; identical shielded plants fill the right half on "share the same defences"; a pin drops on a coded Africa outline on "first found in Uganda"; a rust wash spreads across the field; the shields shatter on "overcame a resistance gene"; the variety row writes "one variety everywhere: shared weakness"
scenes.holdPurpose: Hold the source chip over the field

scenes.visualReference: Potato tuber plate, clone row plate, Cavendish bunch and banana plantation plates, third scorecard column
scenes.teachingReason: Names cloning as the third option and ties it back to the first video's banana
scenes.narrationCue: copy the winner / pieces of tubers / it is a clone / shares one weakness / Cavendish banana
scenes.motionPurpose: Tuber pieces duplicate into a clone row, identical plants ripple out, disease marks spread along the whole row and the banana plates crossfade in
scenes.onScreenChange: The tuber plate crossfades in with a sprout row duplicating on "pieces of tubers"; "clone: the same alleles" writes on in amber; plants ripple along the row on "uniform crop quickly"; disease marks spread plant to plant on "shares one weakness"; the Cavendish and plantation plates land with a ring on the wilting plants; the third column fills

scenes.visualReference: Scorecard enlarged to a three-column comparison with a balance doodle, amber hand type and four gloss lines in the four criterion colours
scenes.teachingReason: Names the verb evaluate and the criteria only after the student has used them on three methods
scenes.narrationCue: make a judgement using criteria / the things you judge it by / Gain: what does it improve / Variety: does it narrow the gene pool? / for animals, welfare
scenes.motionPurpose: The scorecard enlarges, the verb and its meaning write on large, a balance doodle appears and clears, and each criterion is circled with its gloss in turn
scenes.onScreenChange: "evaluate: make a judgement using criteria" writes on with "criteria: the things you judge it by"; a balance doodle with "worth it?" draws and clears; scribble circles land on the gain, variety, cost and welfare row labels in turn with a short gloss writing beside each; a checklist line "judgement, reasons, weighing, when it would change" writes on

scenes.visualReference: Question card, model answer card 1 (judgement) and card 2 (gain) with two herd icons and a pair of rising lines (illustrative)
scenes.teachingReason: Starts the model Evaluate answer with the judgement first, then the gain with comparison evidence
scenes.narrationCue: Here is a model answer for dairy farming / First, the judgement / worthwhile when many unrelated bulls are used / Second, the gain / similar herds that mate naturally
scenes.motionPurpose: The question writes on, the judgement card writes on with its condition lit, then the gain card fills while two herd icons face each other with two rising lines
scenes.onScreenChange: The question card writes on at the top; card 1 "Judgement" writes on with "worthwhile when" lit in amber; card 2 "Gain" writes on with a green tick; two herd icons face each other on "similar herds that mate naturally" and a pair of rising lines draws with the faster one on the straw herd

scenes.visualReference: Cards 3 and 4 beside the small gene pool tray, amber coin and rose heart, scorecard rows lighting in step
scenes.teachingReason: Adds the variety, cost and welfare cards using the tray the student has already seen
scenes.narrationCue: Third, the variety / the gene pool narrows / Fourth, cost and welfare / lower fertility

scenes.visualReference: Card 5 with a small balance tipping to the risk pan, the tray refilling with six colours, a freezer-and-straw icon and an old-breed cow icon
scenes.teachingReason: Finishes the model answer with the weighing and a verdict that says when, and names the ways to protect variety
scenes.narrationCue: Finally, weigh them / the answer turns on variety and welfare / The verdict / Frozen semen / outcrossing
scenes.motionPurpose: The balance tips to the risk pan, a circle lands on the condition, and the tray refills with six colours as three repair icons appear beside it
scenes.onScreenChange: Card 5 writes on with a balance tipping to the risk pan; a scribble circle lands on "lasts if"; unrelated bulls' beads enter the tray and "outcrossing" writes on; the freezer-and-straw icon and the old-breed cow icon appear with their labels

scenes.visualReference: Two numbered vignettes: a coded sheep outline with a straw and farm icons, and a wheat floret outline with a donor head; no scorecard, tray or hints
scenes.teachingReason: Unseen transfer on a new species and on a plant fault, with every demand and condition visible and no answer cues
scenes.narrationCue: Your turn / one champion ram / Give one benefit of this plan / Suggest why, and name two steps she should add / Pause here to answer

scenes.teachingReason: Explains the benefit, the strongest risk and a change that keeps the benefit, and corrects a one-dose cost mistaken for the risk
scenes.narrationCue: the champion's traits spreading quickly / a narrow gene pool / several unrelated good rams / a cost of one dose
scenes.motionPurpose: The ram's bead colour spreads along the farm icons over ten ticks, a disease icon greys them, three more rams' beads refill the tray, and the wrong chips are crossed
scenes.onScreenChange: The tray replays on the flock board; the ram's colour spreads along the farm icons across the ten-year strip; a disease icon lights the farms grey; a second path adds three more rams' colours and the tray refills with "several unrelated good rams"; the chips "the semen might not work" and a second wrong chip appear crossed; a note says another valid risk is accepted

scenes.visualReference: Vignette two enlarged replaying the floret: P's own pollen, wind-blown pollen, forceps, Q pollen and a bag

scenes.narrationCue: fertilised by P's own pollen / remove P's anthers / cover the flowers with a bag / the problem is which pollen arrived
